channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: ADPF 1339: as mulheres trans e a cota de gênero nas eleições
item.description: ADPF 1339 challenges the inclusion of trans women and travestis in Brazil’s electoral gender quota, but the STF, TSE, and Inter-American Court of Human Rights have already established gender as self-declared, guaranteeing rights like name and gender correction in civil registries. Requiring trans women to run under the male quota contradicts their legal identity and disregards evolving constitutional protections for fundamental rights and equality.

item.title: Eleições: apresentadores têm até esta terça para deixar rádio e TV
item.description: TV and radio presenters planning to run in the 2026 elections must leave their programs by June 30, as required by election law and TSE rules, to prevent unfair advantage from media exposure. Among those who have already stepped down are Silvia Abravanel (PSD, SP), José Luiz Datena (PSB), Sikêra Júnior (invited by Tarcísio de Freitas), and André Marinho (Novo, RJ), who have announced or are articulating candidacies for federal deputy, Congress, or governor of Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Valdemar tem encontro com Michelle Bolsonaro para selar paz com Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL, will meet with Michelle Bolsonaro to mediate the conflict between her and Flávio Bolsonaro, following her public claim that he humiliated and disrespected her in a phone conversation about PL alliances in Ceará. The meeting aims to preserve party unity and prevent the feud from undermining Flávio’s electoral performance, particularly among female voters where Michelle holds sway. Despite the tension, Valdemar reaffirmed his support for Flávio’s 2026 presidential bid and ruled out any discussion of replacing him.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro silencia sobre ataques misóginos de assessor
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has remained silent amid misogynistic attacks by his advisor Paulo Figueiredo, who publicly insulted women, including former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro. This silence persists despite polls showing 58% of Brazilian female voters reject his candidacy, signaling a growing alienation from the female electorate. The strategy may reflect a long-term plan for a 2030 presidential bid, but it clashes with demographic reality, as women constitute 53% of Brazil’s electorate.

item.title: Em pré-campanha, Flávio só presidiu uma sessão da Comissão de Segurança
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), announced as a pre-candidate for president in December 2025, presided over only one of the 14 scheduled sessions of the Public Security Commission (CSP) since then. Of the sessions held, he attended two but presided over only one, on April 28, during which projects not aligned with the bolsonarist 'hard-line' agenda were approved, such as banning limits on women's vacancies in security public contests. He claimed to have acted adequately and listed priority projects in the commission, including penalty increases and funding allocations to municipal guards.

item.title: Reunião entre Valdemar e Michelle deve definir futuro da ex-primeira-dama na campanha de Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto is meeting with Michelle Bolsonaro to determine her role in Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign following her public criticisms of him. The meeting aims to resolve the crisis and confirm her participation in a conservative women's leadership event, seen as key to winning female voters. Her decision will depend on the outcome, potentially signaling reconciliation or deepening the rift.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0: famílias renegociaram R$ 17,5 bilhões em dívidas
item.description: Over 7.5 million Brazilian families renegotiated R$17.5 billion in debt through Desenrola 2.0, achieving an average discount of 80% and enabling nearly 5 million people to leave default registries. Launched on May 4, the program has reached 32.9% of the first edition’s total (R$53.2 billion) and will run for 90 days. Including FIES and corporate modalities, total debt renegotiation reaches R$41.6 billion.

item.title: Desenrola, crédito para estudantes, garantia do FGTS: Lula amplia pacote de ‘bondades’ antes do prazo eleitoral
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched Desenrola Adimplentes, a new branch of the debt renegotiation program, targeting informal workers who are current on payments but seek lower interest rates, with debts up to R$15,000 and a monthly rate of 1.99%. The package expands credit measures ahead of the 2026 electoral deadline, aiming to ease debt burdens for low-income populations.

item.title: Flávio deve manter articulação com Ciro no Ceará e acenar a Michelle em outras frentes, avaliam aliados
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is expected to maintain the PL’s political articulation in Ceará despite pressure to reconcile with Michelle Bolsonaro, as allies believe backing down now would signal weakness and undermine his authority in the pre-campaign. The PL leadership, led by Valdemar Costa Neto and supported by Damares Alves, is mediating the conflict with hopes of a private meeting between Flávio and Michelle later this week, contingent on her agreement. Although Jair Bolsonaro urged his son to seek conciliation, family tensions remain high, indicating that a political—not familial—solution is needed to stabilize the presidential pre-campaign.

item.title: Presidente do Paraguai decreta feriado após vitória na Copa
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña declared a national holiday following Paraguay's penalty shootout victory over Germany in the 2026 World Cup, securing a spot in the round of 16. The decree was issued during the 68th Mercosul summit in Asunción, where Brazilian President Lula will announce an increase in Brazil's contribution to the Focem fund from $70 million to $100 million annually over 10 years.

item.title: Reflexos da Copa no jogo eleitoral
item.description: The World Cup and Brazilian elections are often seen as separate spheres of public life, but there are subtle connections between them, particularly around themes of national identity and collective mobilization. Although no specific candidates are mentioned, the text suggests that global events like the World Cup can influence the political and electoral climate, distracting or redirecting voter attention. The reflection argues for viewing these spheres as interconnected, not isolated, in the context of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Com a presença de Janja, PT aposta em encontro com católicos a três meses da eleição
item.description: The PT holds its first National Catholic Encounter in Brasília, with confirmed attendance by First Lady Janja and party national president Edinho Silva, three months ahead of the 2026 elections. The event aims to strengthen the party’s support among Catholics, a segment where Lula leads with 53% according to a recent Datafolha poll, compared to 40% for Flávio Bolsonaro. The PT avoided discussing moral issues like abortion and same-sex marriage, focusing instead on the common good, social justice, and defending the poor, as stated by the party’s inter-religious sector coordinator, Gutierres Barbosa.

item.title: Pauta-bomba: Alcolumbre marca votação de PEC de R$ 30 bi no Senado e põe governo em alerta
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has scheduled a vote today on a PEC granting special retirement benefits to community health agents and endemic disease combat workers, with an estimated fiscal impact of R$ 30 billion over 10 years. The proposal, already approved by the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee, could be fast-tracked in two rounds today, intensifying pressure on public finances and raising government alarms amid a streak of congressional defeats.

item.title: Paga dívida em dia, mas quer renegociar? Entenda as regras do Desenrola para adimplentes
item.description: The government launched Desenrola Adimplentes, a program offering debt renegotiation for informal workers with up to R$15,000 in current debts, provided they have paid at least four installments on time and have no delays exceeding 90 days. The program allows reducing interest rates to a maximum of 1.99% per month (11% per year), with loans offered by Banco do Brasil and Caixa, guaranteed by the FGO, maintaining or extending the original term, and prohibiting betting on 'bets' for six months.

item.title: Mercosul: Lula chega ao Paraguai em cenário político desfavorável no continente e em meio a debate sobre acordos comerciais
item.description: President Lula arrived in Paraguay for the Mercosul summit amid a politically unfavorable regional context, marked by the rise of right-wing forces in Peru and Colombia, although these countries are not permanent members of the bloc. The summit will discuss trade agreements with Panama, the Dominican Republic, Guyana, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago, as well as formalize negotiations with Japan and India. Brazil also announced an annual contribution of US$100 million to the Focem to fund infrastructure and regional development within Mercosul.

item.title: Lula libera R$ 520 mi para propaganda antes da eleição, mais que o dobro de Bolsonaro em 2022
item.description: The Lula government allocated R$ 520 million for propaganda in the first half of 2026, more than double the spending by the Bolsonaro administration in the same period of 2022. The increase in expenses occurred just before the start of Lula’s re-election campaign, signaling a strengthened institutional communication strategy ahead of the elections.

item.title: CNJ tem novos conselheiros negros, mas ainda patina em diversidade
item.description: The CNJ appointed new Black counselors, advancing racial representation, but still falls short of achieving full diversity, with few Black women in leadership roles. Minister Edson Fachin highlighted the absence of a Black woman on the STF, lamenting that President Lula ignored the historic nomination. Despite symbolic progress, institutional structures remain marked by racial and gender inequalities.

item.title: Estratégia do PT em MG é “desastre político”, diz campanha de Marília
item.description: José Prata Araújo, economist and coordinator of Marília Campos' Senate pre-campaign, criticized the PT's strategy in Minas Gerais to launch its own gubernatorial candidacy as a 'recklessness' and 'political disaster', advocating for a broad front with a center-party candidate. He argued that Marília's gubernatorial run would unite the right and benefit Governor Mateus Simões (PSD), while harming Lula's re-election prospects in the state. Marília Campos resists pressure to run for governor, stating she resigned as mayor of Contagem specifically to run for the Senate.

item.title: Pesquisa BTG/Nexus mostra duplo desafio de Lula na disputa com Flávio
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula leading with 42% in the first round and 47% in the second round against Flávio Bolsonaro (34% and 44%, respectively). The first challenge is convincing non-polarized voters (about 20% of the electorate), who are volatile and currently lean slightly toward Lula. The second challenge is turning voting intention into actual turnout, as Lula’s lead shrinks to just one point when considering only voters who participated in the last two presidential elections, signaling a risk of unequal abstention that disproportionately affects his lower-income base.

item.title: Governo cede ao Congresso e envia proposta que eleva faturamento anual MEI para R$ 140 mil até 2028
item.description: The federal government has submitted a bill to Congress raising the MEI's annual revenue cap from R$ 81,000 to R$ 110,000 in 2027 and R$ 140,000 in 2028, while allowing up to two employees at minimum wage. The proposal lacks offsetting revenue measures for an estimated R$ 4 billion loss over two years and may create an actuarial deficit exceeding R$ 90 billion over 70 years due to the MEI's unsustainable 5% contribution rate. It does not alter the Simples Nacional threshold (R$ 4.8 million) and will be debated in a special committee before the July 18 legislative recess.

item.title: A atitude de Flávio no caso Michelle que ‘caiu bem’ para eleitor, segundo CEO de instituto de pesquisa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's conciliatory response to criticism from Michelle Bolsonaro was perceived as a sign of moderation and humility, which 'went well' with part of the electorate, particularly men and 'alternative bolsonarists', helping preserve his competitiveness in the presidential race. According to Marcelo Tokarski, CEO of Nexus, the controversy did not cause the expected electoral damage, and the senator maintained 44% voting intention against Lula's 47% in a return to the 2022 polarization scenario.

item.title: ‘Noite das astronautas’: Michelle Bolsonaro reposta vídeo com relato de festa de Vorcaro
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro’s wife shared a video from ex-governor Anthony Garotinho claiming he saw unverified material about a sex party organized by banker Daniel Vorcaro, where foreign women wore space helmets and were selected by politicians lifting their visors. The post comes amid a rift between Michelle and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who is linked to the jailed banker, and uses biblical quotes as indirect messaging. Garotinho, a Rio gubernatorial candidate, had his conviction annulled by the STF in March and regained political rights.

item.title: O tempo da Justiça e a velocidade da mentira nas eleições de 2026
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian election faces a growing challenge from AI-generated disinformation that spreads faster than electoral justice and platforms can respond. Even when false content is later detected, its impact has already occurred, especially in polarized environments where manipulated messages reinforce preexisting beliefs without needing to convince the majority. AI does not create polarization but exploits it with precision, scale, and speed, making professional communication structures essential to detect and mitigate harm before it becomes irreversible.

item.title: Pesquisa: os grupos que fizeram a diferença entre Lula e Flávio encurtar
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows stability in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, with Lula maintaining 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro oscillating between 33% and 34%. Despite the margin of error, the gap in a potential runoff narrowed from six to three percentage points, driven mainly by voters classified as 'bolsonarists by alternative' - those who reject Lula but are not convinced Bolsonarists.

item.title: Saiba como pode ficar a nova lei para MEIs
item.description: President Lula has sent to Congress a bill to raise the MEI (Microindividual Entrepreneur) revenue cap from R$81,000 to R$110,000 in 2027 and R$140,000 in 2028, allowing up to two employees per business. The proposal also permits temporary hiring during legal absences (e.g., maternity leave), maintains the unified monthly tax payment, and ties the increase to forecasted revenue loss in budget laws per the Fiscal Responsibility Law, with staggered implementation: structural changes effective January 2027, revenue caps from January 2028.

item.title: Damares vira novo alvo de ataques de aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF), an ally of Michelle Bolsonaro and advisor to Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) government plan, has become the target of misogynistic attacks orchestrated by his allies, including Oswaldo Eustáquio and Paulo Figueiredo. The attacks include vulgar language, sexual innuendos, and accusations that she 'wants to destroy the nation,' despite her support for the candidate. Flávio Bolsonaro has not publicly defended her following the attacks.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Haddad mira interior para tentar conter Tarcísio
item.description: Finance Minister Fernando Haddad is intensifying his campaign efforts in Brazil's interior to counter the rising popularity of São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas ahead of the 2026 elections. His strategy aims to strengthen the Workers' Party's base in regions traditionally dominated by the right, focusing on economic issues, employment, and public services to counter Tarcísio's appeal among conservative and agribusiness voters.

item.title: Valdemar tentará convencer Michelle de que racha com Flávio pode custar a eleição ao PL
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto will attempt to convince Michelle Bolsonaro that her split with Flávio Bolsonaro could cost the party the 2026 presidential election, warning that losing her support would make victory 'very difficult'. He previously made similar claims, arguing that disunity would benefit Lula and keep Jair Bolsonaro ineligible for another ten years. The rift stemmed from a video in which Michelle accused Flávio of humiliation and disrespect, though his allies downplay the impact, citing stable internal polling among women and evangelicals.

item.title: Lula faz 1ª reunião com Teresa Leitão, nova líder do Governo no Senado
item.description: President Lula met with Senator Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), the new Government leader in the Senate, in their first meeting since her assumption of office. The discussion focused on the government's priority agenda and political alignment in the Senate, with Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães in attendance. Leitão noted she is the first woman to hold the position and stressed the need to advance policies benefiting the Brazilian people.

item.title: Milei diz a Flávio que “onda azul” chegará ao Brasil neste ano
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei told Senator Flávio Bolsonaro he believes a 'blue wave' of conservative right-wing movements will reach Brazil in 2026, during a meeting at the Casa Rosada. Flávio described Brazil’s October election as 'the missing piece' in the right-wing map of Latin America and framed recent right-wing victories as a rejection of left-wing governments.

item.title: A mando de Lula, Múcio vai a Caracas para articular ajuda à Venezuela
item.description: Defense Minister José Múcio will travel to Caracas on Tuesday (30/6) to coordinate humanitarian aid for Venezuela following two earthquakes that caused 1,719 deaths, over 5,000 injuries, and nearly 16,000 missing. The Brazilian delegation includes officials from Caixa, the Ministry of Cities, and other agencies focused on housing and relief. Additionally, the government is preparing a fifth humanitarian flight carrying medical supplies, equipment, and personnel to support the field hospital in La Guaira.

item.title: Caiado deve anunciar vice na próxima quarta (1º/7): "Curiosidade permanece"
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) said he will announce his running mate for the 2026 election next Wednesday (July 1st) at 11 a.m. at the party’s national headquarters. He declined to reveal whether the vice-presidential pick would be a man or a woman, stating only that the decision is already made and 'the curiosity remains'. Gilberto Kassab, national president of the PSD, is mentioned as a leading contender after offering to discuss the possibility.

item.title: Pesquisa Nexus indica que 22% dos eleitores de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro decidem voto por rejeição ao adversário
item.description: The Nexus poll shows that 22% of voters for Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro make their choice primarily due to rejection of the opposing candidate, reflecting a pragmatic voting pattern driven by aversion. This indicates that for a notable share of the electorate, the decision is less about affirmative support and more about avoiding the candidate deemed unacceptable.

item.title: Brasil anuncia US$ 100 milhões anuais para fundo do Mercosul
item.description: Brazil announced it will allocate US$100 million annually to the Structural Convergence Fund of Mercosul (Focem), reinforcing its commitment to reducing inequalities among member states. The announcement was made by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira during the CMC meeting in Asunción and will be formalized by President Lula at the Mercosul Summit. The fund finances infrastructure projects such as roads, energy, and sanitation, with Brazil currently contributing around 70% of the total resources.

item.title: A Copa derrotou a polarização política e resgatou o verde e amarelo
item.description: The 2026 World Cup united Brazilians around the green and yellow jersey, overcoming political polarization and reaffirming national symbols as belonging to all, regardless of ideology. The text argues that the spirit of unity seen in the stadiums should be carried into the October elections, encouraging conscious voting, fighting corruption, and monitoring officials, irrespective of their political affiliation.

item.title: O impacto da crise familiar: Como a ala ideológica reagiu ao atrito entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Influencers Paulo Figueiredo and Oswaldo Eustáquio publicly exposed the rift between Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro, intensifying a family crisis that is fracturing the ideological base of Bolsonarism. The statements deepened the split within the digital militia, with radical opposition sectors exploiting the conflict to undermine the movement's cohesion.

item.title: Quem são os brasileiros que prometem não votar neste ano, segundo nova pesquisa
item.description: A Nexus/BTG Pactual poll released on June 29, 2026, shows that 3% of Brazilian voters say they have decided not to vote in the October 4 first-round elections, with higher rates among women (4%), those aged 60 or older (4%), voters with only elementary education (4%), evangelicals (6%), those earning up to one minimum wage (4%), and residents of the Southeast (4%). In 2022, over 32 million voters abstained in the first round, or 20.9% of the electorate. The survey interviewed 2,009 voters between July 26 and 28, with a two-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Michelle deixa de seguir Carluxo e Eduardo nas redes
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro unfollowed her brother-in-law Carlos Bolsonaro and her brother Eduardo Bolsonaro on social media after sharing a June 24 video in which she described being treated with hostility by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during a discussion about political formation. The move suggests a possible rift within the Bolsonaro family, with potential implications for the group's political cohesion ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: CNJ divulga ranking de transparência e 20 órgãos do Judiciário atingem nota máxima
item.description: In 2026, 20 Brazilian Judiciary bodies achieved the maximum score in the CNJ's Transparency Ranking, up from 19 in the previous edition. These include seven state justice tribunals, seven regional labor tribunals, four regional electoral tribunals, the TRF-2, and the CSJT. The CNJ itself scored 96.3%, while four bodies fell below 90%, with TRT10 at the lowest with 86.6%. The ranking evaluates 83 questions across 11 themes, and bodies have five days to appeal scores before the final results are published.

item.title: Valdemar defende Michelle na eleição após atrito com Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, met with Michelle Bolsonaro to address the fallout from a video in which she accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of mistreatment. The meeting aims to reinforce her support for the party in the 2026 elections following internal tensions within the Bolsonaro clan. Valdemar acknowledged uncertainty about the electoral outcome but seeks to preserve party unity.

item.title: Com atritos na família, Michelle deixa de seguir Carlos e Eduardo
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro unfollowed her stepsons Eduardo and Carlos Bolsonaro on Instagram after posting videos in which she said she felt humiliated and stabbed in the back by her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president. Despite an apology from Flávio and mediation efforts by the PL party, Michelle maintained the unfollow of Eduardo and Carlos while still following Flávio, as Eduardo publicly criticized her on X. The family rift also included Michelle posting biblical verses seemingly referencing the situation.

item.title: Presidenciáveis celebram vitória do Brasil; Flávio Bolsonaro usa número de Martinelli e Lula posa com Janja
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates celebrated Brazil's victory over Japan in the 2026 World Cup. Flávio Bolsonaro linked Martinelli's goal (wearing number 22) to the PL party's ballot number, while Lula posed with Janja and ministers wearing the Brazilian Paralympic Committee jacket. Other candidates, such as Romeu Zema and Renan Santos, also commented on the match, tying it to political narratives.

item.title: CNJ lança ferramenta de IA para identificar litigância abusiva
item.description: The CNJ announced the launch of Atalaia, an AI tool to identify patterns of abusive litigation in the judiciary, with presentation scheduled for June 30, 2026. The system cross-references data from various courts to detect repetitive, standardized, or weakly documented actions, serving as a support tool for judges without replacing their decision. The initiative reflects the growing use of AI in the Brazilian judiciary, with 66% of courts having AI projects under development in 2023, according to a CNJ survey.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: 'Perfis fantasmas' impulsionam conteúdos pagos contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A report reveals that fake social media profiles are being used to amplify paid content attacking Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 elections. This strategy aims to artificially create a negative perception of the candidate through disinformation and algorithmic manipulation. Digital platforms are under investigation for potential electoral law violations and improper data use.

item.title: Republicanos avalia punição a Manga após vídeo em sede do União Brasil em Sorocaba
item.description: The Republicans party is considering punishing Sorocaba's mayor, Rodrigo Manga, after he posted a social media video showing the União Brasil headquarters decorated with his photo and that of his wife, Sirlange Maganhato, a federal deputy candidate for União Brasil. National party president Marcos Pereira said there is a strong internal movement due to a clear sense of betrayal, as Manga was elected and re-elected under the Republicans banner. Manga said he was unaware of the dissatisfaction, reaffirmed his respect for Pereira, support for his wife’s candidacy, and stated he has no intention of leaving the party, despite facing judicial proceedings for corruption, money laundering, and fraud tied to Operation Copia e Cola.

item.title: Vieira: Mercosul é "baluarte de liberdade" em meio ao protecionismo
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that Mercosul is a 'bulwark of liberty' amid global protectionism, emphasizing its role in promoting trade and free movement of people. He warned against unilateral initiatives undermining the spirit of the Treaty of Asunción and advocated for a transparent, equitable distribution of EU-Mercosul tariff quotas that do not deprive the bloc's productive sectors of their benefits.

item.title: Irmãos Bolsonaro devem responder por incentivarem atos típicos de guerra contra o Brasil
item.description: The article argues that brothers Eduardo and Flávio Bolsonaro could be held legally accountable under Law 14.197/2021 for incentivating acts typical of war against Brazil by supporting U.S. policies such as tariffs and designating criminal factions as terrorists. These actions allegedly constitute negotiation with a foreign government to harm the democratic rule of law, with penalties potentially doubled if belligerent consequences follow.

item.title: Jogou Bem ou Jogou Mal? Heróis da classificação, Martinelli e Bruno Guimarães são eleitos os melhores; Paquetá é o pior
item.description: Gabriel Martinelli was voted Brazil's best player against Japan with 94.31% approval after scoring the winning goal in the 50th minute of the second half. Bruno Guimarães ranked second with 89.16% for the assist, while Lucas Paquetá received the worst rating at 33.78% due to an injury that forced his substitution at halftime. Despite the positive result, the 'Jogou Bem ou Jogou Mal' voting remains open for GLOBO readers.

item.title: DC quer lançar ator Humberto Martins e filha de Roberto Jefferson para deputado federal no Rio
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party plans to launch actor Humberto Martins and Cristiane Brasil, daughter of Roberto Jefferson, as federal deputy candidates for Rio de Janeiro in the 2026 elections, according to Folha de S.Paulo. The strategy aims to leverage the public visibility of these figures to strengthen the party's ticket in the state.

item.title: Lula comemora vitória do Brasil contra o Japão: "Parabéns à Seleção"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated Brazil’s 2-1 victory over Japan in the World Cup, praising the team’s effort and expressing national pride. He watched the match at the Palácio da Alvorada with First Lady Janja and government ministers. Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro highlighted the coincidence that the goal scorers wore jerseys numbered 13 and 22 — matching the ballot numbers of the PT and PL — using it to criticize Lula on social media.
